svg.title: Grounding a Data Agent: Raw-Schema NL2SQL vs Ontology-Grounded NL2Ontology
svg.desc: A contrast diagram with two paths from the same natural-language question. The raw-schema path has the agent's source-specific generator (NL2SQL, NL2DAX, or NL2KQL) translate directly against lakehouse, warehouse, or semantic model schema, relying on developer-authored instructions and example queries to disambiguate business terms — a lever community practitioners repeatedly identify as the biggest driver of answer accuracy, and one that degrades as schema and business vocabulary drift apart. The ontology-grounded path has NL2Ontology translate the same question against a published ontology's entity types and relationships first, then federated query routing pushes the resulting structured query down to whichever backend holds the data. Both paths converge on the same governed, read-only execution and layered precedence controls a Fabric data agent always enforces.
svg.text: Grounding a Fabric Data Agent — Without vs. With a Fabric IQ Ontology

g.title: Natural-language business question — The same question enters either the raw-schema or the ontology-grounded translation path.
g.text: Same natural-language question, two very different paths to a query

svg.text: Business question: "Which shipments are at risk from a cold-chain breach this week?"
WITHOUT an ontology — prompt + raw schema

g.text: 1 · NL question sent with raw table/column names
Model sees column names like Ord_Hdr, Shp_Fact, SnsrLog —
no declared meaning, units, or relationships to lean on.
2 · NL2SQL infers joins and filters freely
The LLM guesses which columns join Order to Shipment to
sensor data, and what "breach" or "this week" means numerically.
3 · A domain expert must manually translate
Every business question otherwise requires a person who knows
both the schema and the business meaning to check or rewrite it.
4 · Fragile, one-off query

g.title: Governed, read-only execution — Both paths converge here: least-privilege execution under the requester's own credentials, read-only only.
g.text: Definitions of "breach", join paths, and units are re-derived (and
may drift) every time the question is asked, by any experience.

svg.text: No shared vocabulary means every question is re-translated by
hand, with no guarantee two people — or two agents — mean the
same thing by "customer" or "breach." Errors surface as wrong
WITH a Fabric IQ ontology — concepts, not columns

g.title: Source-specific generator (NL2SQL / NL2DAX / NL2KQL) — Translates the question directly against raw source schema — NL2SQL for lakehouse/warehouse, NL2DAX for semantic models, NL2KQL for KQL databases.
g.text: 1 · NL question resolved against published entity types
"Shipment," "Order," "sensor reading" already exist as entity
types with standardized names, ids, and properties.

g.title: NL2Ontology — Translates the same question against a published ontology's entity types and relationships, not raw schema.
g.text: 2 · NL2Ontology, not free-form NL2SQL
Generated filters, joins, units, and validity windows are
constrained to the ontology's own published definitions.
3 · Typed relationships traverse the graph
Order → Shipment → sensor reading follows declared, typed,
directional links — no hand-written join logic per question.
4 · Federated execution routes to the right engine

g.title: Federated query routing — Pushes the ontology-constrained query down to whichever backend actually holds the data.
g.text: The ontology layer pushes the query down as GQL (Graph) or
KQL (Eventhouse) — the agent never needs to know which.

svg.text: Result: consistent, governed, and faster to extend
Cross-domain reasoning via relationship traversal, faster
onboarding because concepts are declared once, and governance
from enforcing the same definitions across every team and app

g.title: Instructions & example queries — The single biggest lever for raw-schema answer accuracy — and a hand-maintained one that degrades as schema drifts.
g.text: that reuses the ontology — not just this one agent.

g.title: Four-layer governance precedence — Tenant policy, then workspace governance, then developer instructions — applied identically regardless of translation path.
g.text: Note: the graph must be enabled at the tenant level and refreshed (manual or scheduled) to reflect new source data.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset.
